brief.headline: Fix the 40% return rate first, then benchmark to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹0.65–0.80 per piece for 28 mm caps at higher volume or looser specs
priceAsk.basis: Open-market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc; verdict says MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec — push for that headroom

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer 15 days instead of current 30 days in exchange for the price cut

brief.financialLeverage: Scorpion publishes no financials, so we cannot see their revenue, profit, or cash picture. Our ₹1.66 L annual spend is tiny — we're not a major customer for them. With no financial data and a small order book, our leverage comes from fixing the quality mess (40% returns cost them money too) and from having five strong alternates ready to quote. Push firmly but not aggressively — the lack of transparency and the high return rate mean we need a second source anyway.

evidence.point: Four out of every ten deliveries from them get sent back
Our annual spend with them is very small
Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps runs ₹0.55–1.20 per piece, typically ₹0.85–0.95
Market verdict says modest headroom exists to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec
evidence.figure: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: Paying 15 days sooner frees up nearly seven thousand rupees for us

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, does pharma bottles and caps — a top second-source lead but verify before RFQ

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader at ₹946.50 Cr revenue, strong and profitable, covers bottles and closures for pharma — a robust alternate lead, qualify before quoting

risks: The 40% return rate is a red flag — poor quality or paperwork issues could disrupt supply and cost us more in rejects and delays; address root cause before placing bigger orders
No public financials means we're flying blind on their stability; a second source is essential in case they fold or can't scale
Our ₹1.66 L spend is tiny for them — we have little volume leverage, so tie any concession to fixing returns and faster payment
Paying 15 days early only frees up ₹6817 for us — make sure the price cut is worth more than that small cash benefit
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to keep working with you, but the 40% return rate is costing both of us — let's fix that first, then talk about a price of ₹0.65–0.80 per cap if we tighten payment to 15 days and raise volume.
